steps: Heat the oil in a kadai on medium and fry the chopped onion for about 3 minutes, until soft and see-through.
Add the garlic and most of the ginger, keeping a few ginger strips aside, and stir for about a minute, until it stops smelling raw.
Add the chopped tomato and cook on medium for 6 to 8 minutes, until it turns into a thick, glossy paste.
Stir in the coriander powder, chilli powder and salt and cook for a minute, until oil shows at the edges.
Add the capsicum, green chilli and a splash of water and cook on medium for 3 to 4 minutes, so the capsicum still has some crunch.
Add the paneer cubes and garam masala and stir gently on low for about 2 minutes, until the paneer is hot.
Crush the kasuri methi over the top, add the ginger strips and coriander leaves, mix and serve hot.
note: All three recipes grind whole coriander seeds and dried red chillies into a kadai masala; here coriander powder and chilli powder stand in for it.
